title: Enduring Best Seller Streak

description.intro:
We are given an array, best_seller, with the title of the most sold book for each day over a given period. We are also given a number k with 1 ≤ k ≤ len(sales).

We need to return whether there is any k-day period where every day has the same best-selling title.
examples:
Output: False
No three consecutive days have the same best seller.

Output: True
Days 3-4 have the same best seller "book3".

Output: False
No two consecutive days have the same best seller.

Output: True
The entire array has the same best seller.
constraints: The length of best_seller is at most 10^6
Each book title has length at most 100

complexity:
Time & Space Analysis
n: the length of the best_seller array
k: the length of the window
Fixed-length window solution:

Time: O(n) - we make a single pass through the best_seller array. Each element is added to and removed from the frequency map at most once.
Extra space: O(k) - we store at most k distinct book titles in the frequency map.
Resetting window solution:

Time: O(n) - we make a single pass through the best_seller array.
Extra space: O(1)
The resetting window solution is more space-efficient.

tests.python:
def run_tests():
  tests = [
      # Example 1 from the book
      (["book3", "book1", "book3", "book3", "book2"], 3, False),
      # Example 2 from the book
      (["book3", "book1", "book3", "book3", "book2"], 2, True),
      (["book1", "book1", "book2", "book1"], 2, True),
      # Edge case - k=1
      (["book1", "book2"], 1, True),
      # Edge case - k=len(best_seller)
      (["book1", "book1", "book1"], 3, True),
      # no same sequence possible
      (["book1", "book2", "book1"], 2, False),
  ]
  for best_seller, k, want in tests:
    got = has_enduring_best_seller_streak(best_seller, k)
    assert got == want, f"\nhas_enduring_best_seller_streak({best_seller}, {k}): got: {        got}, want {want}\n"
    got = has_enduring_best_seller_streak_2(best_seller, k)
    assert got == want, f"\nhas_enduring_best_seller_streak_2({best_seller}, {k}): got: {        got}, want {want}\n"

run_tests()
